text: The Mazda R360 is a kei car manufactured and marketed by Mazda from May 1960 to 1969, serving as the company's first passenger car. It is a two-door coupé with a 2+2 seating arrangement, featuring a rear-engine, rear-wheel-drive layout designed to be inexpensive and lightweight. To achieve its low weight, the R360 used a 2+2 design with a rear seat unsuitable for adults, and its engine, chassis, and components incorporated aluminium and magnesium alloys. The vehicle weighed only 380 kg (838 lb), with acrylics replacing glass for the curved rear windshield and sliding side glass to reduce both weight and cost. The R360 was an immediate success due to its low price, selling 23,417 units in its first year, with a total cumulative production of 65,737 units. Sales declined as the four-seat Subaru 360 captured much of the kei car market, prompting Mazda to introduce the four-seater Mazda Carol (P360) two-door sedan in 1962. Full production of the R360 lasted six years, ending in 1966, though the automatic version remained available as a special order for disabled drivers until 1969. The R360 had a 1,760 mm (69.3 in) wheelbase, was powered by a rear-mounted air-cooled 356 cc V-twin engine producing 16 PS (12 kW) and 2.2 kg⋅m (21.6 N⋅m; 15.9 lb⋅ft) of torque, and could reach a top speed of 84 km/h (52 mph). It featured a 4-speed manual or two-speed automatic transmission, with front and rear suspension using rubber "springs" and torsion bars. Two official variants existed: the KRBB with a 4-speed manual transmission and the KRBC with a 2-speed "TORQ DRIVE" automatic transmission. The standard R360 was available in three exterior colours—Opal Green, Maroon Rouge, and Somerset Blue—while the R360 DeLuxe offered two two-tone options: Blue and Cream or Red and Cream. Interior colour choices were limited to Red or Blue, applied to the seats, carpet, and inner door panels. A pickup truck variant, the B360, was based on the R360 Coupé, using the same 356 cc engine in a front-engine, rear-wheel-drive layout with a rigid rear axle and leaf spring suspension; it was upgraded to the Carol's 358 cc I4 engine in 1964 and replaced by the Mazda E360 in 1967. A larger B600 pickup was introduced for the export market, using a 577 cc version of the Mazda V-twin engine.
